# CamBridge — Your iPhone is already a cinema camera. Bridge it to your Mac.

> Full-text homepage content for LLM consumption. Canonical page: https://mohsin.se/cambridge-site/

## Overview

You don't need a $1,000 camera rig. You need CamBridge.

Your iPhone already has a cinema-grade camera. Your Mac is already your studio. CamBridge connects them — so you can see your framing big while you record alone, tap your Mac screen to refocus mid-take, and switch between vertical and horizontal without touching a single cable.

- iPhone beta (TestFlight): https://testflight.apple.com/join/xmwz6mKR
- Mac beta (TestFlight): https://testflight.apple.com/join/X9Hu9RXx
- Free beta — join now.
- Roadmap note: hardware-encoded HEVC streaming is on the roadmap for a sharper, lower-bandwidth preview — recording itself never depends on the network: it's real 4K, on-device, on your iPhone, today.

Device pairing shown on the page: iPhone on a small tripod, vertical, connected live to CamBridge Studio on the Mac showing the same shot big and horizontal (orientation follows whatever the iPhone is doing).

## Live demo

An unedited walkthrough: iPhone on the stand, CamBridge Studio on the Mac — live monitoring, remote controls, and footage landing in the folder.

## Built for creators who ship daily

No fake numbers, no logos we haven't earned yet — just who this is for and what it's meant to make easier.

- **Daily uploaders**: Talking-head videos, vlogs, and shorts don't leave room for a two-hour rig setup. CamBridge is on in under a minute, every time.
- **Podcasters on camera**: Frame yourself properly, see it big on your Mac while you record, and stop squinting at a phone propped up across the room.
- **Course & tutorial makers**: Refocus mid-explanation without breaking your flow — tap the shot on your Mac instead of walking over to the phone.

## Connected in under a minute (setup)

1. **Open CamBridge on your iPhone** — Prop your iPhone up (a small tripod, a stand, or leaning against something) and open the app.
2. **Open CamBridge on your Mac** — Open the Mac app on the same Wi‑Fi and your iPhone shows up automatically. No pairing codes.
3. **You're connected — start shooting** — Your shot appears big on your Mac in seconds, with full control ready to go.

## Everything you need to shoot alone, well (features shipping today)

Once you're connected, your Mac becomes the control room. Your iPhone stays put on its tripod while you drive the shot from your desk.

- **See yourself big** — Your iPhone's shot appears full-size on your Mac, so you can actually see your framing while you record alone — no more squinting across the room.
- **Start and stop from your desk** — Trigger a photo or start recording on the iPhone without walking over and touching it. Stay in your seat, stay in the moment.
- **Tap to focus from your desk** — Click anywhere in the Mac preview to pull focus on the iPhone — exactly like tapping the screen, without leaving your chair.
- **Switch lenses instantly** — Jump between wide, ultra-wide, and telephoto on the fly, right from the Studio window on your Mac.
- **Zoom without walking over** — Smooth zoom control driven live from your Mac's trackpad or a slider — dial in the shot mid-take.
- **Fill light on demand** — Toggle the iPhone's torch for a bit of fill without breaking your shot to reach for the phone.
- **Exposure, dialed in live** — Adjust exposure compensation on the fly and watch the change reflected instantly on your Mac.
- **Shoot vertical or horizontal** — Turn your iPhone and the Studio feed follows instantly, full frame — TikTok and Reels one take, YouTube the next.
- **Bring your own mic** — Pick any mic your iPhone can see — including the DJI Mic directly over Bluetooth (no receiver needed) or via its receiver for full quality — plus USB, wired, and Bluetooth headsets. Switchable from your phone or your Mac, with a live level meter.
- **Footage lands on your Mac** — Hit stop and the real recording — full-quality 4K from the iPhone, not a screen grab — moves itself into your chosen folder on the Mac, ready to edit.

Everything above is live in the beta right now — including real 4K files auto-transferred to your Mac.

## Every orientation. Not just one. (the money shot)

Camo and Blackmagic Camera lock you into landscape. Shoot a vertical TikTok or Reel and you're fighting the app. CamBridge doesn't care which way you're holding your iPhone.

- **Competitors**: Landscape only — rotate the iPhone for a vertical reel and the feed breaks or crops.
- **CamBridge**: Vertical for TikTok and Reels, horizontal for YouTube — the same rig, no re-mounting.

## Searching for a fix? You probably landed here from one of these

If any of this sounds familiar, CamBridge was built for exactly this.

- **Continuity Camera forces my vertical video into landscape 16:9** — Apple's Continuity Camera auto-rotates, stabilizes, and crops vertical footage into a horizontal frame — great for webcam calls, useless for TikTok and Reels. CamBridge streams the true portrait frame straight from the iPhone. Nothing gets rotated or cropped.
- **QuickTime only shows my iPhone camera in landscape** — Since Sonoma, using your iPhone as a camera source in QuickTime on macOS locks the preview to landscape, no matter how you're holding the phone. CamBridge is a native Mac monitor that follows your iPhone's actual orientation — vertical stays vertical.
- **How do I take photos with my iPhone from my Mac?** — See what the iPhone's camera sees, full-size, on your Mac. Tap the preview to pull focus, click a button to fire the shutter — true tethered shooting from your desk, no walking over to the phone.
- **iPhone Mirroring won't open the Camera app** — iPhone Mirroring is built for everyday apps, not live camera control — the Camera app simply isn't supported. CamBridge is built exactly for this gap: full remote camera control from your Mac, with a real live feed.
- **Camo, EpocCam, or Blackmagic Camera didn't solve it** — Camo and EpocCam turn your iPhone into a webcam feed — EpocCam doesn't even do video for photos, and neither gives you real remote control. Blackmagic Camera's remote is iPhone-to-iPhone or iPad, not Mac. Screen Mirroring just takes over your whole display. CamBridge gives you real Mac-side remote control and real 4K files, recorded on the iPhone itself.
- **Remote control my iPhone camera from my MacBook to record myself** — Put your iPhone on a tripod or a tall stand, walk back to your desk, and drive the whole shot from your MacBook — framing, focus, zoom, exposure, and the shutter, all without touching the phone again.

## Why not just use… (comparison)

Camo Studio and Blackmagic Camera are both real products, both worth trying. CamBridge exists because neither one gave us portrait AND landscape monitoring with real, full remote control from the Mac — so we built it.

Comparison reflects our understanding as of August 2026 — check each product for current details.

## No accounts. Nothing leaves your room. (privacy)

CamBridge Camera and CamBridge Studio talk to each other directly over your local Wi‑Fi network. There's no sign‑up, no server in the middle, and nothing about your shoot leaves your network. Built in Swift, kept simple on purpose — what happens in your room stays between your iPhone and your Mac. Full privacy page: https://mohsin.se/cambridge-site/privacy.html

## What's next in the beta (roadmap)

In active development — not yet shipped, no promised dates. Everything here is honestly labeled Coming Soon until it ships.

- Multi-phone grid — monitor and switch between several iPhones at once.
- Use a second iPhone as the director's monitor and remote.
- USB cable streaming, for when Wi‑Fi isn't an option.
- HEVC streaming for a sharper preview at lower bandwidth.

## FAQ — straight answers, no marketing spin

**Do I need Wi‑Fi, or can I use a cable?**
Right now CamBridge needs your iPhone and Mac on the same Wi‑Fi network. USB cable streaming is on the roadmap for when Wi‑Fi isn't an option.

**Is this a finished app?**
No — CamBridge is currently a TestFlight beta distributed through Apple's TestFlight program. That means Apple has reviewed the build, but it's still in active development, things can change, and you're trying it before general release. Join via the buttons on this page.

**What quality actually gets recorded?**
The real recording is full-quality 4K captured on the iPhone itself, and it's auto-transferred to your Mac when you stop. The live preview you see on your Mac while shooting is a separate, lighter monitoring feed — not the file that gets saved. Don't judge final quality by the live preview.

**Does it work with my DJI wireless mic?**
Yes — two ways. Connect the DJI Mic directly over Bluetooth (no receiver needed) and CamBridge uses it as the recording mic, or plug its receiver into the iPhone for the highest audio quality. One honest physics note: Bluetooth mic audio is voice-call quality on any app — the receiver path always sounds better. The mic's on-body record button reaches the phone only through the receiver (in Bluetooth-only mode DJI's button controls the mic's internal recorder, not your phone — that's a DJI hardware behavior, true in every app).

**Does anything leave my network?**
No. CamBridge has no accounts, no sign-up, and no cloud server in the middle — your iPhone and Mac talk directly over your local Wi‑Fi. See the privacy page for details.

**What devices does this need?**
An iPhone running iOS 17 or later, and a Mac running macOS 14 or later (Apple silicon or Intel).

**Does it cost anything?**
It's free during the beta. We don't have final pricing figured out yet — when that changes we'll be upfront about it, and people testing it now will be treated well. No specific promises beyond that.

**How do I report a bug or give feedback?**
Email mohsin.sapra@gmail.com — real feedback from beta testers directly shapes what gets built next.

**How can I use my Mac to remotely take photos with my iPhone?**
Open CamBridge Camera on your iPhone and CamBridge Studio on your Mac — the live view shows up big on your Mac, you can tap anywhere in the preview to focus, and click the shutter button from your desk to trigger the photo on the iPhone. No accessories, no cables required.

**Why does my vertical iPhone video turn horizontal on the Mac (Continuity Camera / QuickTime)?**
Apple's Continuity Camera and QuickTime's iPhone camera source are built around a landscape webcam feed — since macOS Sonoma, they auto-rotate, stabilize, and crop vertical footage into 16:9 horizontal. CamBridge is a different kind of app: it's a dedicated Mac monitor and remote control for the iPhone camera, so it streams and shows the true portrait frame with no rotation or cropping.

**Is CamBridge a webcam app like Camo or EpocCam?**
No. Camo and EpocCam turn your iPhone into a webcam feed for calls and streams. CamBridge is a remote camera and monitor system — the recording you get is the real 4K camera file saved on the iPhone itself, then auto-transferred to your Mac, not a lower-quality webcam stream.
